Package dev.px.core.render

Interface Render3D

public interface Render3D
The world-space drawing backend.

Separate from Render2D because the two have genuinely different implementers. A 2D vector library such as NanoVG or Skija has no concept of a camera, a depth buffer, or a sphere in world space, so it can never implement these. This is supplied by the version adapter, which is the only code that knows how the game sets up its projection.

All positions are absolute world coordinates. The backend subtracts the interpolated camera position itself, so callers never deal with render offsets.

    • worldToScreen

      Vec2 worldToScreen(Vec3 position)
      Projects a world position onto the screen.
      Returns:
      screen coordinates in the same scaled space Render2D uses, or null when the point is behind the camera. Returning null rather than an off-screen coordinate is deliberate: a projected point behind the viewer comes back mirrored, which is how nametags end up drawn on the wrong side of the screen.

    • project

      Render3D.ScreenBounds project(Box box)
      Returns:
      the screen-space bounds of a world box, or null if fully behind the camera.

    • getCameraPosition

      Returns:
      the interpolated camera position this frame.

    • setDepthTest

      void setDepthTest(boolean enabled)
      Whether subsequent draws respect the depth buffer.

      Off is how a box is drawn through walls; leaving it off by accident is why ESP sometimes renders over the GUI, so the backend must restore the previous value in endFrame().
